findings: Four equally dimensioned stool legs reach ground and seat. Apron rails and lower stretchers join the legs; seat bottom equals leg top at .410m. Mallet head bottom equals seat top at .445m and its handle enters the head.

Separate chisel has overlapping handle/ferrule/blade connections and a planar beveled tip. Its illustrative scale and ground placement were inspected from six views. No person, hand grip or instruction sequence is depicted.

Handling tray has a closed base, joined rim and thin mat. Camera body bottom .023m equals mat top. Lens components are coaxial and attached to camera front; shutter button contacts the top cap. Material sample rests on the mat and its grooves remain surface-attached.

Handling sign meets its supported foot at tray rear. Its five-digit handprint is a planar symbol, not a human hand posing over an artifact. Camera and material sample are representative of touch collections.

The three other designs are direct planar speech/music symbols. Whole final projections and all six views were inspected; no material geometry defect was observed. These observations are not exhaustive collision or material simulation.

references.finding: Presenter demonstrates historical furniture construction and hands-on woodworking with antique tools; chairs/benches and joints are explicit. The stool is a generic representative furniture form.
Museum staff facilitate handling selected cameras, life masks and workshop materials; generic camera/material examples ground the tray without promising a fixed collection.
